Subject: NexaCare — post-call recap and RAG evaluation next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Jordan and Sana. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same playbook.

Key takeaways from our discovery:
- Scope: Customer support KB + policy docs ~120k short docs, mostly PDF -> HTML-extracted text.
- Primary goals: 1) Accurate grounding for answers to regulatory questions; 2) low hallucination on medication/policy excerpts; 3) 95th-pctl latency target <= 600ms for single-turn queries.
- Sensitive data: PHI will be redacted before indexing, but some QA flows require token-level auditing.
- Success criteria for pilot: grounding-precision@1 >= 0.85, hallucination-rate < 5% on curated prompt set.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) We will deliver a benchmark pack (prompt sets, eval harness, baseline benchmark report) and a retrieval config proposal by EOD Monday. Attached: nexacare_promptset_v1.csv and nexacare_benchmarks_v1.pdf.
2) Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60-min session next week for your infra and our SEs to validate embedding/DB options.
3) Pilot matrix: 1 week of eval runs using your snapshot of content + our recommended model/reranker configs.

Tentative roles and ownership:
- Redwood (Marissa, Karthik): provide eval artifacts, run pilot, and surface performance/cost tradeoffs.
- NexaCare (Jordan, Sana): provide one-time content export and a small list of 100 gold QA pairs for quality baselining.

If that all looks right I will: 1) drop the benchmark pack to the shared drive; 2) propose 3 time slots for the deep-dive.

Best,

Evelyn Hart | Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: NexaCare — post-call recap and RAG evaluation next steps (baseline models & targets)

Jordan — quick note from the SE side with recommended baselines for the pilot and the metrics we'll report.

Model candidates (tradeoffs summarized):
- Redwood-3-small (8-bit) : best latency / cost balance, good for throughput; expect slightly lower long-tail factuality on rare policy excerpts.
- Llama-3-13B-int8 : stronger factual recall on longer context, higher cost and latency.
- Safety fallback: run a smaller instruction-tuned decoder for short deterministic lookups (low-cost path).

Embedding + retrieval:
- Embedding: text-embedding-3-small (or equivalent production embedding in your VPC)
- Vector index: FAISS HNSW with PQ for dense storage (we'll include a config yaml attached)
- Chunking: 500 token overlap, 1k token max chunk size for long PDFs to keep provenance tight.

Reranker recommendation:
- Two-stage: bi-encoder candidate retrieval + cross-encoder reranker (roberta-large-msmarco-style). This reduces noise and improves grounding-precision@1.

Target metrics we'll measure in the pilot (and thresholds):
- grounding-precision@1 >= 0.85
- exact-match@1 >= 0.78 on curated pairs
- hallucination-rate <= 5% (manual annotation sampling)
- avg latency (99th-pctl) <= 650ms for single-turn queries on recommended infra

Costs: rough compute estimate for 1-week pilot (processing 120k docs + running 5k eval queries):
- Redwood-3-small baseline: ~12 GPU hours (A10-class equiv) + embedding compute; approx $950 in infra run cost.
- Llama-3-13B-int8 baseline: ~28 GPU hours; approx $2,300 in infra run cost.

I'll drop the detailed benchmark PDF and the retrieval config file to the drive link that Evelyn mentioned.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachment stubs: nexacare_retrieval_config.yaml (YAML), nexacare_benchmarks_v1.pdf (linked)

Subject: NexaCare — tech plan and eval steps (pilot runbook)

Jordan — following up with the concrete runbook we propose for the 1-week pilot. Please review and flag anything that won't map to your infra.

1) Data ingest (day 0):
- NexaCare delivers S3 export or drive folder. Preferred: S3 layout with document_id, source_url, raw_text, metadata.json. Drive folder OK for the first run.
- We will run an automated redaction pass to remove explicit PHI fields before indexing.

2) Indexing (day 0-1):
- Chunking: 500 token chunk size, 128 token overlap for provenance. (Marissa suggested 500/overlap; we recommend 128 overlap to avoid too much index growth.)
- Embedding model: text-embedding-3-small. Index: FAISS HNSW with 128-d PQ, efConstruction 200.

3) Retrieval config to test (we'll run as variants):
- Variant A (latency optimized): top_k=10 bi-encoder candidates, rerank top 5 with cross-encoder; MMR disabled.
- Variant B (precision optimized): top_k=50 bi-encoder, rerank top 20; MMR with lambda=0.7 to reduce redundancy.

4) Prompting and context windows:
- System prompt template and three candidate answer templates attached in the CSV prompt set.
- Use strict provenance injection: include 2 most relevant chunks with source citations in the answer format.

5) Evaluation:
- Run 5k eval queries (from your 100 gold pairs + synthetic augmentations).
- Metrics captured: grounding-precision@1, exact-match@1, rouge-l, per-query latency, and manual hallucination sample.

6) Deliverables (end of week):
- Benchmark report with per-variant metrics and cost delta.
- Prompt tuning recommendations (3 suggested templates).
- Exported index snapshot + seed scripts for reproducibility.

Links: HubSpot deal NX-7832 (https://hubspot.example.com/deal/7832) and shared drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cNexaCareEval). Pilot start proposed Wednesday 26 Aug if NexaCare can deliver content by Monday evening.

If that works I'll set up the SE deep-dive for tomorrow or Wednesday.

Cheers,
